near_duplicate_resolution.resolution: Retain V2-Q1387 as the bank's enoxaparin prefilled-syringe self-administration item using the current branded FDA label. V2-Q0653 will be rebuilt into a different pharmacology construct.

semantic_correction.stem: The nurse asks a client to demonstrate self-administration of Lovenox from a prefilled syringe. Which technique demonstrates correct understanding?

options.A: Expel the air bubble, inject into an abdominal skin fold, alternate left/right sites, and avoid rubbing afterward.
options.B: Keep the air bubble, insert the full needle into an abdominal skin fold, alternate left/right sites, and avoid rubbing afterward.
options.C: Keep the air bubble, insert the full needle into an abdominal skin fold, use the same site for each dose, and avoid rubbing afterward.
options.D: Keep the air bubble, inject into an abdominal skin fold, alternate left/right sites, and massage the site afterward.

semantic_correction.rationale: The current FDA-approved Lovenox label instructs deep subcutaneous administration, states not to expel the air bubble from a prefilled syringe, directs alternating left and right abdominal-wall injection sites, instructs insertion of the whole needle into a skin fold held throughout the injection, and advises not to rub the site afterward to minimize bruising. Option B contains those source-supported elements. Option A incorrectly removes the air bubble. Option C incorrectly reuses the same site instead of alternating sites. Option D incorrectly massages the injection site after administration. Therefore B is the uniquely correct technique.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Teach safe Lovenox prefilled-syringe self-administration by retaining the air bubble, using a subcutaneous abdominal skin fold, rotating sites, and avoiding rubbing after injection.
semantic_correction.source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. Food and Drug Administration labeling; Sanofi-Aventis U.S. LLC
semantic_correction.source_document_title: LOVENOX (enoxaparin sodium) injection — Full Prescribing Information

semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: For Lovenox prefilled-syringe subcutaneous injection, do not expel the air bubble; alternate abdominal injection sites; insert the full needle into a skin fold and hold the fold throughout injection; do not rub the site afterward.

audit_findings_append.finding: V2-Q1387 and V2-Q0653 tested essentially identical enoxaparin prefilled-syringe technique. Q1387 was retained, but all distractors were rebuilt as clinically plausible technique bundles and the source was refreshed to the current branded FDA label.

option_audit.A: Plausible because the remaining site and aftercare elements are appropriate, but the FDA label directs the client not to expel the prefilled-syringe air bubble.
option_audit.B: Correct. It combines the label-supported air-bubble, full-needle skin-fold, site-rotation, and no-rubbing instructions.
option_audit.C: Plausible because the air-bubble and skin-fold steps are correct, but the FDA label directs alternating abdominal sites rather than using the same site for each dose.
option_audit.D: Plausible because the air-bubble, abdominal route, and site rotation are appropriate, but the label instructs not to rub or massage the site after injection.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. Each distractor contains one specific label-inconsistent technique while B contains the complete source-supported combination.

cueing_check.note: All options are parallel multistep self-injection techniques; the correct answer is not the longest and no filler was used for mechanical equality.
